content: Pepto-Bismol is an over-the-counter medication manufactured by the Procter & Gamble company. It is primarily used to address minor disturbances in the digestive system. The active ingredient in Pepto-Bismol is bismuth subsalicylate. This medication is effective in alleviating symptoms such as nausea, heartburn, indigestion, upset stomach, diarrhea, and other temporary discomforts affecting the stomach and gastrointestinal tract. Pepto-Bismol is available in chewable tablets and swallowable caplets, but it is most widely recognized for its original formulation, which is a thick liquid. This original liquid form is characterized by its medium pink color and a strong wintergreen flavor. These distinctive traits have become so closely associated with the product that the terms Pepto-Bismol pink or tasting like Pepto-Bismol are sometimes used descriptively. However, these associations are often viewed negatively due to the unpleasant connotations of the medication and the general discomfort linked to stomach issues. The product is also colloquially referred to as pink stuff. Historically, Pepto-Bismol was initially marketed as a treatment for infant diarrhea by the Norwich Pharmaceutical Company under the name Bismosal: Mixture Cholera Infantum. In 1919, the product was renamed Pepto-Bismol. Later, in 1982, the brand became part of Procter & Gamble following their acquisition of Norwich Eaton Pharmaceuticals.
